SD-2026-SB204.title: revise certain criteria for loans from the South Dakota housing infrastructure fund.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Commerce and Energy

SD-2026-SB204.aiSummary: The law revises some rules for loans from the South Dakota housing infrastructure fund. It affects people or groups that seek loans from that fund.

SD-2026-HB1264.title: eliminate the Agricultural Land Assessment Implementation and Oversight Advisory Task Force, and to provide that the Department of Revenue receive the submission of recommendations and provide a report on agricultural value.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Agriculture and Natural Resources
First read in House and referred to House Agriculture and Natural Resources

SD-2026-HB1264.aiSummary: The bill became law in South Dakota. It ends the Agricultural Land Assessment Implementation and Oversight Advisory Task Force and shifts the job of receiving recommendations and reporting on agricultural land value to the Department of Revenue.

SD-2026-HB1220.title: regulate the sale of nicotine products, and to provide a penalty therefor.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Health and Human Services
First read in House and referred to House Health and Human Services

SD-2026-HB1220.aiSummary: This law would regulate the sale of nicotine products and set a penalty for breaking those rules. It affects people and businesses that sell nicotine products in South Dakota.

SD-2026-HB1187.title: add coaches to the list of mandatory reporters of child abuse or neglect.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Judiciary
First read in House and referred to House Judiciary

SD-2026-HB1187.aiSummary: The bill adds coaches to the list of people who must report suspected child abuse or neglect. It affects coaches and the people who may make those reports. It was signed by the governor.

SD-2026-HB1077.title: consider a cultivated-protein food product to be adulterated food.

actions.text: Delivered veto sustained to the Secretary of State
First read in Senate and referred to Senate Agriculture and Natural Resources
First read in House and referred to House Agriculture and Natural Resources

SD-2026-HB1077.aiSummary: The bill would have treated a cultivated-protein food product, a food made from grown cells, as adulterated food under state law. It would have affected makers and sellers of those products in South Dakota. The governor vetoed it, and the veto was not overturned.

SD-2026-HB1066.title: revise a provision related to theft by a contractor, subcontractor, or supplier.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Judiciary
First read in House and referred to House Judiciary

SD-2026-HB1066.aiSummary: This bill would change a rule about theft by a contractor, subcontractor, or supplier. It affects people and businesses in those roles, and it was signed by the governor.

SD-2026-SB60.title: restrict ownership of real property interests by certain prohibited entities and to provide for enforcement.

actions.text: First read in House and referred to House Military and Veterans Affairs
First read in Senate and referred to Senate Commerce and Energy

SD-2026-SB60.aiSummary: South Dakota SB 60 would limit certain barred groups from owning real estate interests and set rules for enforcing that limit. It passed the Legislature and was signed by the Governor, so it became law.

SD-2026-HB1099.title: reschedule the pharmaceutical composition of crystalline polymorph psilocybin in a drug product approved by the Food and Drug Administration as a Schedule IV controlled substance.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Health and Human Services
First read in House and referred to House Health and Human Services

SD-2026-HB1099.aiSummary: The law changes the drug schedule for crystalline polymorph psilocybin when it is part of an FDA-approved drug product, placing it in Schedule IV, which is a lower-control drug category. It affects that specific psilocybin drug product in South Dakota and became law when the governor signed it.

SD-2026-SB82.title: prohibit the misrepresentation of an animal as a service animal and to provide a penalty therefor.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Judiciary

SD-2026-SB82.aiSummary: This law makes it illegal to say an animal is a service animal if it is not. It also sets a penalty for that kind of false claim. The rule applies to people who misrepresent an animal as a service animal.

SD-2026-HB1253.title: adjust the assessment methodology for owner-occupied single-family dwellings and nonagricultural property.
SD-2026-HB1253.aiSummary: The bill would change how certain homes and nonfarm property are assessed for tax purposes in South Dakota. It moved through the House Taxation Committee with amendments, but the amended version later failed in that committee.

SD-2026-HB1176.title: clarify bond or pre-trial release upon sobriety program participation.

actions.text: Placed on calendar pursuant to JR 6F-6, Failed (Y 8, N 26)
Report out of committee without recommendation as amended, Passed (Y 5, N 4)
Referred to Senate Committee on Appropriations, Passed (Y 6, N 1)
First read in Senate and referred to Senate Judiciary
First read in House and referred to House Judiciary

SD-2026-HB1176.aiSummary: The bill would clarify how bond or pre-trial release works for people taking part in a sobriety program. It would affect people going through the court process who are in that program.

SD-2026-HB1143.title: authorize the possession and self-administration of diabetes medications by a student on school property and at school-related events and activities.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Health and Human Services
First read in House and referred to House Health and Human Services

SD-2026-HB1143.aiSummary: Allows a student to have and use diabetes medicine on school grounds and at school events or activities. It affects students with diabetes and school staff who oversee those settings. The bill was signed by the governor.

SD-2026-SB138.title: revise the time within which a recount for a school board election must be completed.

actions.text: First read in House and referred to House Education

SD-2026-SB138.aiSummary: The measure changes the deadline for finishing a recount in a school board election. It affects school board election recounts in South Dakota and has been signed by the governor.

SD-2026-SCSC821.title: honoring Arthur Mauf for his dedication and service to the United States as he approaches his 100th birthday.
SD-2026-SCSC821.aiSummary: A South Dakota resolution would honor Arthur Mauf for his dedication and service to the United States as he approaches his 100th birthday.

SD-2026-SB71.title: authorize the assumption of certain responsibilities and the waiver of sovereign immunity in connection with certain actions under federal environmental law.

sponsor.name: The Chair of the Committee on Transportation at the request of the Department of Transportation

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Transportation

SD-2026-SB71.aiSummary: South Dakota passed and the governor signed a bill that lets the state take on certain duties and give up its claim to immunity in some cases under federal environmental law. It applies to actions tied to those federal rules.

SD-2026-HB1022.title: revise and repeal provisions related to the crime victims' compensation program.

sponsor.name: The Chair of the Committee on Judiciary at the request of the Department of Public Safety

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate Judiciary
First read in House and referred to House Judiciary

SD-2026-HB1022.aiSummary: The measure updates and removes some rules for the state crime victims' compensation program, which helps people affected by crime. It was passed by lawmakers and signed by the governor.

SD-2026-SB93.title: prohibit certain state officers or employees from being employed by an organization that was the recipient of a contract awarded on behalf of a state agency for a period of time.

actions.text: First read in Senate and referred to Senate State Affairs

SD-2026-SB93.aiSummary: The bill would bar certain state officers and employees from working for an organization that got a contract from a state agency for a set time. It affects some state workers and groups that receive state contracts.

SD-2026-SB116.title: make an appropriation for the design and construction of an indoor athletics facility at Dakota State University and to declare an emergency.

actions.text: First read in House and referral to committee waived pursuant to JR 6D-1
First read in Senate and referred to Joint Committee on Appropriations

SD-2026-SB116.aiSummary: The law provides money to design and build an indoor athletics facility at Dakota State University. It affects the university and the state funds used for the project. It also declares an emergency, so it takes effect right away.

SD-2026-HB1275.title: create requirements for age verification and parental consent for application stores and to provide a penalty therefor.

actions.text: Deferred to the 41st legislative day, Passed (Y 5, N 4)
First read in Senate and referred to Senate State Affairs
Prime Sponsor Changed at the Request of the Prime Sponsor
First read in House and referred to House State Affairs

SD-2026-HB1275.aiSummary: This bill would set rules for app stores to check a user's age and get parental consent for minors before some apps can be downloaded. It would affect application store operators and people under the age limit, along with their parents or guardians. It would also add a penalty for not following those rules.

SD-2026-SJRSJR502.title: applying to the United States Congress under Article V of the United States Constitution to call for a convention proposing an amendment to the constitution fixing the number of justices of the United States Supreme Court at one chief justice and eight associate justices.

actions.text: Deferred to the 41st legislative day, Passed (Y 12, N 0)
First read in Senate and referred to Senate State Affairs

SD-2026-SJRSJR502.aiSummary: This resolution would ask the U.S. Congress to call a convention under Article V of the Constitution. The goal would be to propose an amendment that sets the U.S. Supreme Court at one chief justice and eight associate justices.

SD-2026-SB215.title: provide for a pilot program for the implementation of a secured cryptographically end-to-end verifiable voting system in certain jurisdictions.

actions.text: Withdrawn at the Request of the Prime Sponsor
First read in Senate and referred to Senate State Affairs

SD-2026-SB215.aiSummary: The bill would have set up a pilot program to try a secured voting system in some areas. The system would use cryptography, a way to protect and check data, to help voters verify votes end to end. The bill was withdrawn at the request of the prime sponsor.
